subject: Evening surge — hosted streaming chat p99 spike (SSE) — emergency plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir.p@quickassist.com>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 16:05:12 -0800
Subject: Evening surge — our hosted chat p99 rising during 6–8pm PT

Logan —

We're seeing severe tail latency on the hosted streaming chat (SSE) tonight between ~18:05 and 18:45 PT. p95 is elevated but p99 responses are taking 2.5–3.2s for streaming connect + first bytes; messages drop mid-stream ~4% and we see a spike in 500s (gateway timeout). This is affecting our live support routing. Attached a small set of session IDs and error snippets.

Quick notes from our side:
- Traffic pattern: 2.8x baseline for 18:00–18:30 window
- We did not change client config
- We rely on hosted API endpoint: api.redwood.ai/v1/stream/chat

We need an ETA and mitigations — our CS teams are on standby. Can we get an emergency plan?

—Samir
Senior SRE, QuickAssist
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@quickassist.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 16:18:33 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evening surge — our hosted chat p99 rising during 6–8pm PT

Samir —

Thanks for the data and the session IDs. We're on it and treating this as P1. I've looped in SRE (Karthik) and CS lead (Marissa). Initial actions we're taking immediately:

1) Enabling burst capacity for your tenant (QuickAssist) — buys short-term headroom.
2) Flipping routing policy to prefer eu-central fallback for new sessions that accept region fallback (will not migrate in-flight).
3) Toggling conservative batching (lower batch size) for streaming paths to reduce queueing risk; we'll watch cost impact.

Can you confirm whether any tenant-level network rules would block eu fallback? If not, expect the routing flip to start within 6–8 minutes.

I'll update in 15m with telemetry.

—Logan
Principal Account Engineer
Redwood Inference
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 16:34:58 -08:00
Subject: RE: Evening surge — hosted streaming chat p99

Agree on the immediate actions. Quick diagnostics from infra:
- Autoscaler observed abrupt queue depth increase on pooling layer for sse-streamer nodes 13–17 18:02–18:22 PT.
- Several nodes hit socket accept stalls (ephemeral) followed by connection timeout bubbling up as 502/504 at the edge.
- KV cache hit-rate dropped ~18% for that window (evictions during burst).

Short-term mitigation I'm doing now:
- Replacing affected streamer nodes with fresh instances (rolling restart) to clear accept backlog.
- Enabling temporary model-variant fallback for streaming: route to quantized-16 variant with same topology (slight quality risk) to reduce per-token compute.
- Applying a conservative ingress throttle to prevent chaotic retries from amplifying load (50% of observed retry rate).

I'll monitor p99 telemetry and post a status shortly. If those don't drop p99 within 12 minutes, we escalate to exec-level mitigation (global canary rollback of last runtime kernel change).

—Karthik
SRE Manager, Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@quickassist.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 16:46:01 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evening surge — hosted streaming chat p99 rising during 6–8pm PT

Samir —

Update: we enabled burst capacity and started router preference to eu (customers who accept fallback). Early telemetry shows p95 improved but p99 remains elevated (around 1.6–1.9s). We're now:

- Completing streamer node replacements (60% done)
- Active routing to quantized-16 streaming variant for 37% of sessions (small quality A/B)
- Engaging logging-level increase for accept path to capture socket traces (will add noise; keeping timeboxed)

If you can, please hold off aggressive client-side retries for 20 minutes while we stabilize — retries make tail worse. I'll ping when we have sustained p99 < 1.0s for 10 minutes.

—Logan
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 17:05:20 -08:00
Subject: Re: Evening surge — hosted streaming chat p99

Thanks — looping in a short exec note for visibility.

TL;DR: QuickAssist experiencing sustained p99 regression during evening peak; SRE has enacted node replacement, region fallback, and model-variant routing. Current mitigation is holding but p99 above target.

Action items for leadership / FYI:
- Ops: Continue aggressive node rotation + validate kernel selection revisions from today's runtime push (rollback candidate).
- Product: Prepare customer-facing summary and proactive credit offering if service-levels not met (estimated impact window 30–90m).
- CS: Reduce client retry guidance and notify support queue to de-escalate.

Marking as exec-notify; will update in 30m.

—Marissa
Head of Customer Success
Redwood Inference
From: Logan Wright <logan.wright@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Patel <samir.p@quickassist.com>, ops@quickassist.com
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 05 Dec 2028 19:12:04 -08:00
Subject: Final update: evening stabilization and next steps

Samir —

Final update for this incident window:
- p99 for streaming connect and first bytes dropped to ~0.92s sustained for 20m after completing node replacements and increasing burst capacity; error rate down to 0.6% (from 4.2%).
- We rolled back a kernel selection tweak that had been promoted in the last runtime push as a rollback candidate; telemetry indicates improved accept latency after rollback.
- We will run a focused retrospective with infra and runtime teams tomorrow morning to harden the accept path and KV eviction behavior.

As follow-ups:
- I'll share a condensed incident write-up and attach the sanitized trace bundle (perf_trace_20281205.zip).
- Marissa will reach out about a goodwill credit if post-checks show SLA breach.
- We recommend adding an explicit region-fallback flag in your client to allow smoother rerouting during future bursts.

Thanks for the quick coordination — please reopen the thread if anything resurfaces.

—Logan
Principal Account Engineer
Redwood Inference
